chosen_leak: In-app: role picked -> pressed Create (the occasion/examples screen + the message box, index.html #buyerSection/#receiverSection -> #createSection). Of the warmest users in the whole funnel, ~39% who pick a role never press Create (Supabase 30d linked: role_selected -> create_clicked 55 of 90 = 61%; 14d: role_selected 63 -> create_clicked 38 = 60%). The entire loss falls between picking a role and reaching Create (role_selected -> message_written is the same 55/90 = 61%, since Create fires with the message write).
why_highest_impact: Traced to REVIEWS this beats every other open leak on value-per-recovered-user, which is what matters once you are past a gate. Reviews are the only goal, and this window 9 of 9 review clicks (30d: 20 of 21) came from the in-app thank-you screen, which appears only AFTER a finished video; email_redirect and preview/share produced ~0. So reviews are gated by getting users to a finished video, and pressing Create is essentially the finish line: create_clicked -> video_started = 55/59 = 93%, and video_started -> review ~= 30%. Therefore recovering ONE role-committed user to press Create is worth ~0.93 x 0.30 ~= 0.28 reviews - the highest per-person review yield anywhere in the funnel, because these users have already survived every earlier gate (they scanned, paid the email price, auto-forwarded in at 97%, and committed to a role). Compare an email-gate recovery: 0.98 (cta) x ~0.37 (in-app arrived->create) x 0.93 x 0.30 ~= 0.10 reviews per recovered scanner - roughly a third the value, and many of those are one-off gift buyers who will never place the 'next order' the discount rewards. The claim email gate loses more raw headcount (287->123) and sits higher in the funnel, BUT (1) its dominant cause is now known to be first-paint NON-engagement (this window only ~38% even engage the field; 84% of engagers submit) - exactly what the two 2026-07-23 attacks (warm-voice rewrite + character-portrait hero) targeted, on top of PR #8; and (2) it was attacked with 3 distinct mechanisms, last just 3 weeks ago. The other in-app sub-step (arrived->role) was shipped against on 2026-08-01 (the 'quiet the inbox exit' welcome re-rank), so it is freshly fenced. That leaves role->Create as the single highest-value leak inside the review engine that is genuinely under-worked: the occasion/examples screen has NEVER been attacked, and the message box has exactly ONE flat mechanism against it (2026-07-06 pre-fill default + NAME-landmine fix), which fences only that mechanism.

angles.angle: Above-the-fold Create: make the primary CTA persistently visible
angles.mechanism: On the message screen (#createSection) the gold '✨ Create Video' button (#generateBtn) is a normal in-flow submit sitting BELOW the textarea AND below a full 'SELECT CHARACTER' card of nine thumbnails - it is not sticky and not fixed, so on a phone the one action a ready-to-go warm user wants is off-screen until they scroll past a nine-item grid. Give the message screen a persistent, refined bottom CTA bar (the same gold button, docked and always in view) so the moment a user is satisfied with the pre-filled message they can commit without hunting. Pure prominence/position change; the message box, character card and Create action are all untouched in function.
angles.cause_addressed: Friction / weak CTA prominence: warm, already-sold users can't see or reach the button at the moment they're ready, because it lives below the fold behind a nine-way character grid.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: #generateBtn is in-flow after the nine-thumbnail #products carousel; no position:sticky/fixed exists anywhere in index.html. The default message is auto-filled, so many arrivals need nothing except to press the button - which they can't see. Concrete structural flaw, not a feelings guess.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The only prior message-step attempt (2026-07-06) changed the textarea DEFAULT and removed the NAME alert - it never touched the button or its position. Distinct from the 'Lever 3' welcome hero (2026-06-16) and the 2026-08-01 welcome re-rank (both on the welcome screen, above role-pick). Touches no gate, reward, or step.
angles.on_brand_fit: More premium, not less: a calm docked CTA removes the below-the-fold scramble and reads as confident and considerate; no new emoji, no hype, nothing removed.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: restyles/repositions the existing #generateBtn into a sticky CTA bar on #createSection; no copy, step, character choice, gate, or reward changed.

angles.angle: Rebuild the occasion screen around one obvious forward tap
angles.mechanism: The occasion/examples screen (#buyerSection/#receiverSection) is a horizontally scrolling video carousel where tapping a card only PLAYS the video (handleExampleClick) - a dead end for progression - while the real way forward is either a small '📝 Customize Template' button on a card or a 'Create from Scratch' button hidden below an 'or' separator. Replace the carousel-of-players with a clean vertical set of 2-3 outcome cards where the WHOLE card is the forward action (tap -> straight to the message screen with that message pre-filled), and drop the ambiguous 'or / from scratch' fork. One screen, one obvious path onward.
angles.cause_addressed: Choice/affordance confusion: the tap target that feels primary (the video) doesn't advance, and the actual 'next' actions are small, competing, and partly below the fold - so users stall on the first screen after committing to a role.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: handleExampleClick just plays with sound; advancing needs 'Customize Template' or a below-'or' 'Create from Scratch'; scroll-snap carousel. This is the FIRST screen after role-pick and it has NEVER been attacked - a strong place for the 39% to be leaking.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Coverage map: the occasion/examples screen has zero prior attempts. Wholly distinct from the 2026-07-06 message-box fix (a different screen) and from every welcome/claim-page change. No owner rejection touches it.
angles.on_brand_fit: Premium: fewer, larger, calmer cards and a single clear action replace a busy carousel with competing buttons and emoji labels ('🎉', '✨ choose your occasion', '📝').
angles.size: Reversible and focused: restructures the two example sections' cards and forward affordance; both roles and their templates stay, no step removed, message screen unchanged.

angles.angle: Collapse occasion into the message screen (one fewer hop)
angles.mechanism: Today role-pick lands on a full occasion INTERSTITIAL (#buyerSection/#receiverSection), then a separate message screen (#createSection) - one guaranteed screen transition whose real job is just to set which template pre-fills the box. Merge them: send role-pickers straight to a ready-to-send message, with the 2-3 occasion/vibe options as light inline chips above the textarea (tap a chip -> swaps the message text). The examples still exist, but as an inline control, not a screen - removing a transition between the warmest users and the Create button.
angles.cause_addressed: Too many steps / transitions: every screen hop after role-commit sheds users, and the occasion screen is an extra hop before they can act, even though the message is auto-filled anyway.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: minimum path is examples-screen -> create-screen (1 transition) even when the user types nothing, because the default message auto-fills. Removing the hop attacks the 39% role->Create loss directly. Magnitude is a bet; the redundant hop is real.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Never attempted. Distinct from 2026-07-06 (changed the default INSIDE the box, not the step count) and from 2026-06-16's email-skip (which removed a DOWNSTREAM email screen for claim users, not the occasion screen). No gate or reward removed - the occasion choice survives as inline chips.
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm and effortless: fewer screens feels more like a gift moment and less like a wizard; the examples remain, just closer to hand.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: folds the example cards into inline chips on #createSection and routes selectBranch straight there; both roles/all templates retained, no step or reward removed.

angles.angle: Show the payoff at the moment of commitment
angles.mechanism: On the message screen the result is invisible - the user sees a textarea and a nine-character grid, and the only explanation of what they'll get ('a video of your character saying your words') is buried inside a collapsed 'ℹ️ How It Works' tooltip. Add a compact, muted, captioned looping example of the FINISHED video (the character actually speaking) beside/above the message box, so while the user reads the pre-filled line they can picture the delightful outcome and feel the press-Create effort is worth it. The magic is demonstrated at the exact commit point, not one screen earlier.
angles.cause_addressed: Unclear/unfelt payoff at the decision point: the video is an unannounced bonus, and at the moment of commitment the screen reads like a form, so users don't feel what they'd get for acting.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: #createSection has textarea + nine-thumbnail grid, no result preview; the example videos live only on the PRIOR occasion screen; the 'created uniquely using AI' reassurance is hidden in a tooltip. Value-demonstration bet, structurally grounded.
angles.why_untried_and_different: The 2026-06-16 'Lever 3' hero was a TEXT value-prop on the welcome screen (pre-role); example videos on the occasion screen are pre-commit. A finished-video preview AT the message/commit step has never existed. Distinct from the claim-page portrait (2026-07-23, different page/asset).
angles.on_brand_fit: Premium and warm: leads with a real, affectionate result rather than emoji claims; the muted captioned loop suits silent mobile viewing and cleans up the form feel.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: adds one small preview element to #createSection (asset already exists as example videos); no step, gate, reward, or character logic changed.

angles.angle: Know their crochet friend: resolve the character from the SKU, drop the nine-way pick
angles.mechanism: The message screen forces a 'SELECT CHARACTER' decision across nine thumbnails, with Potato hard pre-selected regardless of what they actually bought - yet the SKU already identifies the exact crochet friend. Auto-select the correct character from the SKU and replace the nine-grid with a confirmed, personal line ('Your Green Potato will say this') plus a subtle 'use a different character' link for the rare mismatch. Removes a redundant decision, personalises the moment to THIS gift, and shortens the screen so Create sits higher.
angles.cause_addressed: Redundant decision friction + lost personal thread: asking users to pick from nine characters we already know theirs is pointless work, and a generic grid drains the affection for the specific handmade gift that would motivate finishing.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: #products lists nine thumbnails with Potato pre-selected irrespective of SKU; the SKU->character mapping is already resolved elsewhere in the app (PRODUCT_CONFIG / product images swap per product). Grounded that the data exists; the lift is the bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Never attempted. Distinct from 2026-07-06 (textarea default) and from the CLAIM-page character portrait (2026-07-23, a different page and a first-paint hero, not the in-app character selector). No owner rejection applies.
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm and premium: naming the exact handmade friend continues the box's affectionate voice; fewer choices, cleaner screen, no emoji soup.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: pre-selects the SKU's character and collapses the nine-thumbnail grid to a confirm+change control on #createSection; every character still reachable, no step removed.

angles.angle: Reassure effort and quality right at the button
angles.mechanism: Two doubts sit unaddressed at the commit point - 'how much do I have to write?' and 'will an AI video actually be any good?' - and the reassurance that answers them ('one line is enough', 'created uniquely for you', 'ready in 2-3 minutes') is hidden inside the collapsed '🎬 How It Works' tooltip most users never open. Surface a single calm line directly beside the message box / Create button: e.g. 'One line is plenty - we'll turn it into a video of your [character] in about a minute. Free.' Lowers perceived effort and output risk exactly where the decision is made.
angles.cause_addressed: Overestimated effort + output-quality doubt at commit: the message box looks like open-ended writing and the payoff quality is unproven, so warm users hesitate; the answer exists but is buried.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: the effort/quality/timing reassurance is entirely inside a click-to-open tooltip; nothing reassuring is visible at the button. Partly grounded (the copy exists, just hidden); the lift is a bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: Distinct from the welcome 'Free · Takes a minute · No app needed' strip (pre-role, generic, on the welcome screen); this is at the create commit, names the character and the tiny effort, and is on #createSection. Not the 2026-07-06 default-fill mechanism (that changed text INSIDE the box, not visible reassurance).
angles.on_brand_fit: Warm, human, non-pushy: honest reassurance in plain language, no incentive-for-review wording, no emoji.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: adds one microcopy line to #createSection near the box/button; no step, gate, reward, or layout rebuild.

angles.angle: Show the finish line: a quiet 'last step' cue on the message screen
angles.mechanism: The occasion screen carries a 'Step 1' eyebrow, but the message screen (#createSection) has NO step indicator, so after one hop the user faces what looks like open-ended work with no sense of how close they are. Add a refined 'Last step' / 'Step 2 of 2' cue to the message-screen header (pairing with the existing 'Step 1'), so the finish line is visible - people complete what looks nearly done (endowed progress), and the perceived remaining effort drops.
angles.cause_addressed: Overestimated remaining effort / no visible finish line: 'Step 1' with no 'of N' and no 'Step 2' makes the task feel longer than the two taps it actually is.
angles.evidence_hint: Flow map: #buyerSection/#receiverSection show a 'Step 1' subtitle; #createSection header ('Create Your Message') has no step label. Minimum real path from role-pick is 2 taps. Endowed-progress is a classic abandon lever; magnitude here is a bet.
angles.why_untried_and_different: No progress cue has ever been added to this stretch. A prior-cycle endowed-progress idea was aimed at the arrived->role WELCOME stretch and was NOT shipped (2026-08-01 shipped the inbox re-rank instead); this is a different surface (the message screen) and completes the existing 'Step 1' rather than inventing a stepper from nothing.
angles.on_brand_fit: Minimal and premium: a quiet type-based cue, no emoji or hype, fits the clean-hierarchy bar.
angles.size: Reversible and focused: adds a small step cue to #createSection's header to match the existing 'Step 1'; no step added or removed, no reward change.

recommended_pick: Above-the-fold Create: make the primary CTA persistently visible
pick_rationale: It wins on value x confidence x on-brand fit. VALUE: it attacks the purest slice of the leak - users who are already sold (they picked a role and the message is auto-filled) but cannot see or reach the one button that finishes the job, because #generateBtn is a non-sticky, in-flow control sitting below the textarea AND a nine-thumbnail character grid, off-screen on a phone. Every recovered press flows almost straight to a finished video (create->started 93%) and into the thank-you screen that produced 100% of this window's review clicks, at ~0.28 reviews per recovered user - the funnel's best per-head yield. CONFIDENCE: this is not a hypothesis about feelings - the below-the-fold CTA is a verifiable structural flaw in the markup, and the fix (dock the existing button) is small, mechanical, and maximally reversible, so it is buildable and low-risk even at our noise-floor traffic. ON-BRAND: it removes a scramble rather than adding anything, reading as calmer and more premium; no copy, emoji, gate, reward, character choice, or step changes. It beats the runners-up: 'Rebuild the occasion screen' (the strongest alternative, on a never-touched surface with a real affordance flaw - the planner may reasonably prefer it) and 'Collapse occasion into the message screen' both have higher ceilings but are larger, riskier rebuilds at lower confidence; 'Show the payoff' and 'Reassure at the button' rest more on unproven value/motivation bets; 'Resolve the character from the SKU' is strong but a bigger logic change with a mismatch edge case; 'Show the finish line' is the cheapest but lowest-confidence. Cleanly distinct from the one fenced mechanism on this step (the 2026-07-06 textarea default + NAME fix) and from every owner rejection and claim-page attempt.
